# Introduction

The treecrownr package provides a simple way to calculate tree crown area using crown diameter measurements.

Tree crown measurements are useful in environmental science, particularly for studying urban forests and analyzing remote sensing data.

# Installing the Package

Once the package has been installed, it can be loaded using:

```{r}
library(treecrownr)
```

# Calculating Tree Crown Area

The `crown_area()` function calculates the area of a circular tree crown using its diameter in metres.

The formula is:

$$A = \pi \left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2$$

where A is crown area and d is crown diameter.

For example, a tree with a crown diameter of 5 metres has an area of:

```{r}
crown_area(5)
```

The function can also calculate crown areas for multiple trees:

```{r}
crown_area(c(3, 5, 8))
```

# Example Dataset

The package includes a synthetic dataset called `sample_trees`, containing six trees with species names and crown diameter measurements.

Load the dataset:

```{r}
data("sample_trees")
head(sample_trees)
```

# Calculating Crown Area for the Dataset

We can use the crown diameter measurements to calculate crown area for every tree in the dataset.

```{r}
sample_trees$crown_area_m2 <-
  crown_area(sample_trees$crown_diameter_m)

print(sample_trees)
```

# Summary

This vignette demonstrated how to use the treecrownr package to calculate individual tree crown areas and apply the function to an example dataset.

These calculations can support further analysis of tree canopy characteristics.
